subsystems.name: Orbital reconnaissance
subsystems.role: finds and maps the cold traps before anything lands.

subsystems.name: Mobility and power
subsystems.role: gets the drill to a place with no sunlight, so no solar power.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic drill and sampler
subsystems.role: extracts ice-bearing regolith without warming it.

subsystems.name: Cold chain and curation
subsystems.role: keeps the sample below the temperature where volatiles migrate or organics react.

subsystems.name: Organic cleanliness control
subsystems.role: stops the spacecraft itself from contaminating the sample with Earth organics.

subsystems.name: Analytical suite
subsystems.role: identifies what is actually in the ice.

buildSteps.title: Map the cold traps
buildSteps.detail: Orbiters and impact experiments measure hydrogen and reflectance in permanently shadowed craters, where surfaces stay below roughly 110 K — cold enough to trap water and other volatiles for billions of years.

buildSteps.title: Choose a site
buildSteps.detail: Landing must be near the boundary of a shadowed region, where terrain is gentle enough to land and a rover or drill can cross into darkness and back.

buildSteps.title: Build the drill and sample tube
buildSteps.detail: Ice-bearing regolith is as hard as concrete when frozen, so the bit is designed for cold vacuum, and the tube is sealed the moment it is filled.

buildSteps.title: Clean the whole chain
buildSteps.detail: Every surface that touches the sample is baked, solvent-cleaned and monitored, because amino acids at part-per-billion levels are the signal being sought.

buildSteps.title: Land and traverse
buildSteps.detail: The lander touches down on polar terrain, and the rover — powered by a radioisotope source or a large battery, since sunlight never reaches the target — drives to the sampling point.

buildSteps.title: Drill and seal
buildSteps.detail: The bit bores into the cold regolith; the sample is transferred without ever rising above about 200 K, ideally staying far colder, and the container is sealed in vacuum or inert gas.

buildSteps.title: Analyse or return
buildSteps.detail: Either instruments on the rover run evolved-gas and mass-spectrometry measurements, or the sealed container is launched back to Earth and opened in a cold cleanroom.

buildSteps.title: Compare and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Results are compared with carbonaceous meteorites and comet samples to see whether the organics are primordial, and whether any amino acids show a chiral bias.

prerequisites.tech: Precision landing on rugged polar terrain
prerequisites.why: shadowed craters have steep, poorly lit slopes; hazard-avoiding landing has been demonstrated but not routinely at the poles.

prerequisites.tech: Power and thermal control in permanent darkness
prerequisites.why: no solar power is available, and electronics and mechanisms must survive tens of kelvin.
no mission has ever returned material kept cold from collection to laboratory; existing sample-return curation is at room temperature.

prerequisites.tech: Organic contamination control at trace levels
prerequisites.why: planetary-protection cleaning is well developed, but detecting part-per-billion organics requires standards closer to cleanroom semiconductor practice.
evolved-gas analysis and mass spectrometry have flown on planetary missions and can be adapted.

pathway.milestone: orbital and impact measurements have already confirmed water ice in polar cold traps
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of sites worth landing at.

pathway.milestone: robotic landers drill polar regolith and analyse volatiles in situ
pathway.unlocks: first ground truth on what the ice actually contains, beyond hydrogen signatures seen from orbit.

pathway.milestone: a sealed, cold sample is returned from a permanently shadowed region
pathway.unlocks: laboratory-grade chromatography and isotope analysis, including chirality measurements no rover can do.

pathway.milestone: deep drilling into ancient ice layers
pathway.unlocks: a readable record of billions of years of inner-solar-system organic delivery, and a test of whether prebiotic chemistry survives in cold traps.
